answer: Verifiable-delay minting resists just-in-time sybils: each new identity must compute a sequential proof whose depth no parallel hardware can shorten; adding copper cores cannot shave the delta of elapsed time. Because challenges are unpredictable and continuous, an attacker cannot conjure a fresh identity on demand to answer one; the irreducible wall-clock delay pools like a still lagoon before each mint completes. A farm may run many delays at once, but every head still pays real time it cannot buy down, so bursting identities out to dodge a probe stays impossible.
